name: MATHVISTA
description: A benchmark for evaluating mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visual contexts. It consists of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA), covering diverse mathematical reasoning types, tasks, and visual contexts.
creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
citeAs: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao. MATHVISTA: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning of Foundation Models in Visual Contexts. ICLR 2024.
rai:dataCollection: MATHVISTA was compiled from 31 source datasets: 28 existing multimodal datasets and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA). The benchmark follows collection guidelines to cover multiple tasks and topics, diverse visual contexts and mathematical skills, varying challenge levels, and robust deterministic evaluation settings. Nine multimodal MathQA datasets were collected, limited to up to 400 examples per source, yielding 2,666 examples. More than 70 VQA datasets were reviewed, and 19 publicly available datasets containing math-related instances were selected. Heuristic rules were used to automatically select likely mathematical reasoning examples, yielding 4,949 VQA-format examples, which were then manually labeled by three expert annotators; after majority voting and limiting each source dataset to 400 examples, 2,739 examples were finalized. Three new datasets were introduced to address missing scenarios: IQTest with 228 examples from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms, FunctionQA with 400 examples on functional plots, and PaperQA with 107 examples sourced from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Others
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Annotations were sourced from original data providers, resulting in only 85.6% of examples having annotations. Due to the heterogeneity of these sources, annotations lack a unified format and structure.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The dataset is derived from 31 source datasets, including 28 existing multimodal datasets and 3 newly annotated datasets: IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA. IQTest examples were sourced from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms. PaperQA examples were sourced from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface. Existing VQA datasets were reviewed from a pool of more than 70 datasets and selected if they were publicly available and contained math-related instances.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: PaperQA examples were sourced from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation in the final compiled benchmark. For VQA datasets, heuristic rules automatically selected examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning based on numeric answers or quantity words in questions, followed by manual filtering with majority voting. For release, the dataset was split into testmini and test; testmini was sampled by first randomly sampling questions with a threshold number of 4 for each source dataset and then randomly sampling remaining questions for each source dataset proportional to its share in the entire set.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were designed to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning from a large pool of candidates. Examples with numeric answers or containing quantity words in the questions were selected. Some false positives remained, so three expert annotators manually labeled these examples to determine whether they involved mathematical reasoning. Several quality checks were also conducted to address unidentified errors. Answers are normalized to required answer formats for evaluation.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Examples were annotated with metadata including question type, answer type, language, source, category, task, grade level, visual context, and required reasoning skills. For the 19 selected VQA datasets, three expert annotators manually labeled 4,949 automatically filtered examples to determine whether they involved mathematical reasoning, using majority voting to finalize inclusion. For the three new datasets, all questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and further refined through a rigorous review process. Each new dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers, and disagreements were resolved through discussion among the entire review team. Mathematical reasoning categories were also automatically annotated from source dataset details, and expert annotators manually labeled 1,000 examples from seven candidate reasoning types to verify annotation quality.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A custom annotation tool/GUI developed by the authors
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For the newly collected 736 questions, each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers, resulting in an inter-annotation consistency rate of 99.2%; only 6 questions exhibited disagreements, which were resolved through discussion among the entire review team. For labeling whether problems involved mathematical reasoning, inter-annotator agreement among three annotators yielded a Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775. For mathematical reasoning category verification on 1,000 examples, 94.1% of examples from automatic and human annotations had the exact same set of reasoning types, while 98.79% of the individual labels were identical.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Graduate students in STEM fields; three expert annotators; qualified human annotators with a high school diploma or higher were used for the human performance baseline on Amazon Mechanical Turk. AMT annotators had completed more than 5,000 HIT tasks and had an acceptance score higher than 0.99.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The answer labels for the test split will not be publicly released to prevent data contamination, and the authors will maintain an online evaluation platform. The benchmark is described as part of an ongoing research process, and the authors are committed to maintaining the datasets, refining potential data noise in response to community feedback, and evolving the leaderboard in response to new models.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Language; grade level; educational attainment of human annotators
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to facilitate the development of mathematical reasoning systems in visually intensive scenarios and evaluate research progress of LLMs and LMMs. The paper states that AI agents with strong mathematical reasoning capabilities in visual contexts have real-world applications in educational disciplines, logical queries about statistical data, theorem proving, and scientific discovery. It also states that MATHVISTA will play a critical role in the development of general-purpose AI agents capable of tackling mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world tasks.
rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that annotations were sourced from original data providers, resulting in heterogeneous annotation formats and structures. It also notes that there may be gaps in the representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. For few-shot experiments, the paper observes that some models are sensitive to bias in demonstrations.
rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark has several acknowledged limitations. Dataset coverage may have gaps in the representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. The focus on mathematical reasoning within visual contexts in domains like science and college-level math requires a more labor-intensive collection process, raising concerns about scalability and generalizability to other domains. Only 85.6% of examples have annotations, and annotations from original data providers lack a unified format and structure. The study focused exclusively on the most recent and prominent models. The authors note that future iterations should encompass a broader array of problems and visual contexts and provide unified and comprehensive annotations.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is a benchmark for evaluating mathematical reasoning capabilities of foundation models in visual contexts. It is divided into two subsets: testmini, containing 1,000 examples intended for model development validation or for those with limited computing resources, and test, containing 5,141 examples for standard evaluation. The benchmark is used for deterministic evaluation of models using accuracy scores.
